one_month_reasoning: Q3 FY2026 results are the one scheduled event in the window. They are most likely on Wed 2026-10-28: FORM has reported on a Wednesday every quarter (8-K dates 2024-10-30, 2025-10-29, 2026-04-29, 2026-07-29), and the Nov 4 calendar date some sites show is last year's 10-Q filing date, not the release. The date is not yet announced. A beat against the $270M / $0.86 / 54% GM guide is likely. However, about 300bp of that margin guide comes from one-offs: $7-9M of IEEPA tariff refunds (10-Q) plus precious-metal reclaims (call summaries). The Q4 guide will therefore step down toward the ~51% underlying margin, and Farmers Branch costs start moving into COGS as production begins late in Q4 (10-Q). The stock has run ~55-60% in a month on one sell-side note (Deutsche Bank, 9/30), and post-earnings moves have been very large in both directions. I use a one-month sigma of ~23.5% (above the 85%/3.5 baseline because earnings fall inside the window) and put the median at ~$147.5, a touch below the actual $149.15 close, for short-term reversal after the run and the margin step-down. That is close to neutral, not a strong call.

fair_value.method: Blend: forward P/E on NTM EPS at Oct 2027 of $4.15 x 30 plus ~$5/share net cash = $130 (weight 0.6); EV/sales on NTM revenue of $1.35B x 7.5 plus ~$0.40B net cash = $132 (0.25); FCF yield on NTM FCF of ~$270M (~$3.40/share) at 3.0% plus net cash = $118 (0.15). Blended about $128, roughly 13% below the $147.90 brief close.

bear.story: AI/HBM test demand pauses or normalizes in 2027. SK hynix alone was 24.3% of Q2 revenue (29.5% in Q1), and DRAM is about a third of revenue. Technoprobe keeps taking share (H1 +42%, guide raised; TrendForce has it as #1 in 2026), and the Nvidia second source stays small. Gross margin settles near or below the ~51% underlying level as one-offs drop out and Farmers Branch ramp costs land in COGS. NTM EPS of ~$3.20 at ~26x is about $88, near the Aug-Sep trading range. FORM has had two ~60% drawdowns in five years and a 49% high-to-low within 2026.

base.story: Growth continues at ~20-25% and margins hold near 51-52% before Farmers Branch accretion. NTM EPS is ~$4.15-4.30 by Oct 2027, and the multiple compresses from ~48x clean run-rate EPS today toward 30-32x as earnings growth becomes the expected case. The stock ends roughly flat to slightly lower.

bull.story: The Nvidia/TSMC GPU probe-card second source ramps (Deutsche Bank: ~20% share, >$200M by 2028; Nvidia was already a 10.2% customer in Q1 2026). HBM4 test intensity lifts DRAM probe revenue, and Farmers Branch pulls margin toward the 55% target early. NTM EPS of $5+ at 40x+ takes the stock above DB's $200 target.

thesis_break_reason: A close below ~$90 would be under the early-September low ($92) and ~40% off spot, about 21-22x a clean NTM EPS of ~$4.15. Given 85% volatility, a move that large most likely means a fundamental miss, not noise: a Q4/Q1 guide-down showing the HBM/DRAM ramp stalling or an SK hynix order cut (24% of revenue), visible probe-card share loss to Technoprobe, the Nvidia second source failing to materialize, or gross margin settling below the ~51% underlying baseline once Farmers Branch costs hit COGS.

reasoning: Round 2 changes, driven by the supervisor's fact-checks and my re-reading of the Q2 10-Q. (1) The clean-margin adjustment stands: the 10-Q confirms $7-9M of IEEPA tariff refunds, and with metal reclaims the one-offs are ~300bp, so the clean run rate is ~$0.77/qtr (~$3.08 annualized). (2) I misread customer concentration in round 1. The 10-Q Note 2 shows Intel's 12.4% is the Q2 2025 column. In Q2 2026 only SK hynix (24.3%) and TSMC (11.0%) were 10%+ customers (35.3%). I re-checked this myself, and it slightly reduces the concentration risk I flagged. (3) Nvidia was a 10.2% customer in Q1 2026, which partly corroborates the DB second-source thesis, so the bull tail gets a little more weight. (4) My FCF leg was wrong. H1 FY26 OCF was $106.8M and capex only $24.8M (FCF ~$82M), so my earlier $160M FY27 FCF and the 2026 capex range I used were too pessimistic. Rebuilt on ~$270M NTM FCF at a 3% yield, the leg is worth $118, not $80. (5) I re-based NTM EPS at Oct 2027 to $4.15, up from my $4.00 FY28 figure. It stays below the supervisor's $4.30 because I keep weight on two verified facts: Technoprobe's faster growth (guide raised Aug 5) and the 10-Q saying Farmers Branch ramps through FY2027 with start-up costs moving into COGS, which delays margin accretion. The blended fair value rises from $115 to $128, still ~13% below spot. I disagree with moving all the way to $135: I would not pay 32x a margin peak in a stock with two ~60% drawdowns in five years. A new skeptic-lane search found no fresh short report, downgrade or litigation since my round-1 work. The bear case remains valuation and cyclicality, not solvency (debt ~$11.6M, short interest 3-5%). Scenarios: bear $88 (28%), base $140 (47%), bull $220 (25%), mixed as lognormals (sigma 0.30-0.33). That gives a median of ~$136 and P(>=$148) of 0.44, and I fattened the far tails slightly for the 60% drawdown history and the AI-momentum right tail. The actual 10/2 close was $149.15 vs the brief's $147.90; the 0.8% difference does not materially move the ladder.
